solution: If a quadrilateral is a parallelogram, then its opposite angles are congruent.
If a quadrilateral is a rectangle, then its diagonals are congruent.
If a triangle is isosceles, then the segment joining its vertex and the mid point of the base is perpendicular to the base.
If the alternate angles formed by a transversal of two lines are congruent, then the two lines are parallel.
If two lines are parallel, then a pair of the interior angles made by their transversal are supplementary.
If the diagonals of a quadrilateral are congruent, then that quadrilateral is a rectangle.
